title: Overtime and other pay: San Francisco against the largest California cities
question: Is San Francisco’s overtime, and its pay outside salary and overtime, high for a large California city?
finding: Taken whole, no. In 2024 San Francisco paid overtime equal to 10.6% of regular pay, 11,486 dollars per paid position; it ranks 7 of 8 among itself and the 7 largest other city payrolls (Los Angeles, San Diego, San Jose, Long Beach, Oakland, Sacramento, Fresno), whose middle figure is 15.3%. Its overtime share moved from 9.4% in 2019 to 10.4% in 2025. Other pay was 4.9% of regular pay and lump sums 0.5%.
how: State Controller raw export, employer type “City”, years 2019 to 2025 as the export labels them. Sums over every position with wages above zero. Overtime share is overtime divided by regular pay; other pay and lump-sum pay are the export’s own columns. Peers are the seven city payrolls with the most paid positions in 2024. The export does not say whether a year is a calendar or a fiscal year. San Francisco’s overtime here is $480.3 million for 2024; the City’s own payroll file has $468.9 million for fiscal 2024 and $471.0 million for fiscal 2025, so the two sources are close but not the same and are not mixed in any one figure.
limits: San Francisco is a city and a county: its payroll carries hospitals, public health, social services, courts staff and jails that a city payroll does not, and much of that work has little overtime, which lowers the whole-payroll share. Some city payrolls include utilities, ports or airports. A position is a row in the export, not a person: a part-time or part-year position lowers the per-position figure. The department tables that follow compare like with like.
